## `verify_agent_protocol`

Check the Personal Agent Protocol file you published: Last Price fetches https://<domain>/.well-known/poppy.json and compares it with the one get_agent_protocol gives. A match verifies the domain for your workspace; a failure returns reason and message saying what to fix, and a domain another workspace verified answers 409. Answers 404 until agent protocol files are switched on for your workspace. Needs a Last Price credential with routing write scope. Needs a claimed workspace: a sandbox key from self-registration is refused (403) until a person claims the workspace.

- **Access:** key, routing write scope (claimed workspace only: a self-registered sandbox key gets 403)
- **Behaviour:** changes data
- **REST:** `/api/agent-protocol/verify`
- **Errors and cautions:** A match verifies the domain for your workspace; a failure returns reason and message saying what to fix, and a domain another workspace verified answers 409. Answers 404 until agent protocol files are switched on for your workspace.

_No arguments._

## `get_spend_policy`

Read the spend policies your workspace's buyer agents spend under (the most per purchase, a daily cap in UTC days, when a person approves first, which sellers and categories), the defaults a save fills in, and what today's reservations hold. An agent key sees its own policy and the workspace default. Needs a Last Price credential with routing read scope. Needs a claimed workspace: a sandbox key from self-registration is refused (403) until a person claims the workspace.

- **Access:** key, routing read scope (claimed workspace only: a self-registered sandbox key gets 403)
- **Behaviour:** changes data

| Argument | Type | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `agent_id` | string | Optional: also say which policy governs this agent. |

## `set_spend_policy`

Save a spend policy whole: agent_id for one agent, or leave it out for the workspace default every other agent spends under. An omitted field takes its default, so read get_spend_policy first and send every rule you want to keep. An agent's own key cannot change the rules that bind it: use a workspace-wide key. Needs a Last Price credential with routing write scope. Needs a claimed workspace: a sandbox key from self-registration is refused (403) until a person claims the workspace.

- **Access:** key, routing write scope (claimed workspace only: a self-registered sandbox key gets 403)
- **Behaviour:** changes data
- **REST:** `/api/spend-policy`

| Argument | Type | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `agent_id` | string / null | The agent this policy governs. Null or omitted for the workspace default. |
| `currency` | string | Currency of every amount here; purchases in another are denied. Defaults to USD. |
| `max_per_purchase` | number / null | Most one purchase may cost. Null (the default) for no limit. |
| `daily_cap` | number / null | Most all purchases may cost in one UTC day. Null (the default) for no cap. |
| `ask_above` | number / null | Purchases above this wait for a person's approval. Null (the default) for never. |
| `allowed_sellers` | array / null | Only these sellers. Null (the default) for any. |
| `blocked_sellers` | array | Never these sellers. Defaults to none. |
| `allowed_categories` | array / null | Only these categories. Null (the default) for any. |
| `fair_price` | `off` / `ask` / `deny` | When verify_price judges a price too high: off (ignore, the default), ask a person, or deny. |
| `hold_seconds` | integer | How long an allowed purchase's reservation stays open for the purchase to start. Defaults to 900. |
| `preset` | `procurement` / `null` | procurement switches on company buying rules in one step, filling ask_above 500, quotes_required_above 5000 and, with preferred_sellers, block_unknown_sellers for whichever you leave out. Only where get_spend_policy says procurement.available. |
| `preferred_sellers` | array / null | Vendors procurement approved. Another seller waits for a person, or is denied with block_unknown_sellers. |
| `block_unknown_sellers` | boolean | Deny any seller not on preferred_sellers. Defaults to false. |
| `category_monthly_budgets` | object / null | Most spent per category in one UTC month, e.g. {"software": 2000}. Checks must then name a category. |
| `quotes_required_above` | number / null | Purchases above this need quotes from at least two sellers. |
| `require_verified_agent` | boolean | Only agents that prove who they are with an AgentID token on check_purchase may spend. Only where get_spend_policy says verified agents are available. |
| `allowed_agent_subjects` | array / null | Only these AgentIDs (the subject in their token) may spend. Null for any verified or unverified agent the other rules allow. |

## `check_purchase`

Before you pay for something, ask whether your owner's spend policy lets you pay this price to this seller. Works for any purchase, whatever wallet or checkout you pay with. Returns a decision (allow, deny or ask), a reason code and a reason. allow comes with a reservation: the amount is held against today's cap, so make the purchase, then call settle_purchase with outcome paid (and the amount paid) or failed. ask means a person approves first; once they have, send the same check again. deny means do not buy. With include_fair_price, or when the policy asks for it, the price is also judged by verify_price and its verdict and band come back with the answer. Needs a Last Price credential with price compute scope. Needs a claimed workspace: a sandbox key from self-registration is refused (403) until a person claims the workspace.

- **Access:** key, price compute scope (claimed workspace only: a self-registered sandbox key gets 403)
- **Behaviour:** changes data
- **REST:** `/api/spend-policy/check`

| Argument | Type | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `agentid_token` | string | Your AgentID ID token, issued for Last Price, when your owner's policy lets only verified agents spend. Sent as the AgentID-Token header. |
| `seller` **(required)** | string | Who you are paying: a store, domain, API or wallet name. |
| `amount` **(required)** | number | The price you are about to pay. |
| `currency` | string | Three-letter ISO currency code. Defaults to USD. |
| `item` | string | Optional: what you are buying. |
| `category` | string | Optional: its category, when the policy limits categories. |
| `agent_id` | string | Only with a workspace-wide key: check on behalf of this agent. An agent key always checks as itself. |
| `include_fair_price` | boolean | Also judge the price with verify_price and return its band. |
| `quotes` | array | Optional: competing offers for this purchase, yours among them. A procurement policy needs two above its two-quote threshold. |
| `intent` | object | Optional: what the buyer approved for this purchase, from an American Express intent, an AP2 intent mandate, or declared by you. A purchase that names another seller, costs more than max_amount (counting every purchase under the same intent_id), is in another currency or comes after expires_at is denied, whatever the policy allows. evidence (the token or mandate) is kept only as a hash and is not verified yet. Only where the workspace has intents switched on (else an error with code not_released). |

## `confirm_purchase`

Call right before you pay for a purchase check_purchase allowed. If the workspace's owner changed the spend policy since the purchase was approved (a lower maximum, a lower daily cap, a blocked seller), it is checked again under the rules as they stand now. confirmed true: pay now. An error saying the policy changed: do not pay; the hold was released, so check the purchase again. Only while the workspace has confirming switched on (the reservation then names confirm). Needs a Last Price credential with price compute scope. Needs a claimed workspace: a sandbox key from self-registration is refused (403) until a person claims the workspace.

- **Access:** key, price compute scope (claimed workspace only: a self-registered sandbox key gets 403)
- **Behaviour:** changes data
- **REST:** `/api/spend-policy/reservations/{id}/confirm`
- **Errors and cautions:** An error saying the policy changed: do not pay; the hold was released, so check the purchase again.

| Argument | Type | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `reservation_id` **(required)** | string | reservation.id from check_purchase. |

## `settle_purchase`

Close the reservation an allowed check_purchase gave you, once: outcome paid when the purchase went through (send amount when you paid less than reserved; never more), or failed when it did not, which gives the amount back to today's budget. When you cannot tell (the payment timed out or the answer was unreadable), send outcome unknown: the amount stays held, failed is then refused, and reconcile_purchase closes it once you know. A reservation is never released by time alone, so always settle it. Needs a Last Price credential with price compute scope. Needs a claimed workspace: a sandbox key from self-registration is refused (403) until a person claims the workspace.

- **Access:** key, price compute scope (claimed workspace only: a self-registered sandbox key gets 403)
- **Behaviour:** changes data
- **Errors and cautions:** When you cannot tell (the payment timed out or the answer was unreadable), send outcome unknown: the amount stays held, failed is then refused, and reconcile_purchase closes it once you know.

| Argument | Type | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `reservation_id` **(required)** | string | reservation.id from check_purchase. |
| `outcome` **(required)** | `paid` / `failed` / `unknown` | paid: the purchase went through. failed: it did not. unknown: you cannot tell yet. |
| `amount` | number | With paid: what you actually paid, if less than reserved. |
| `note` | string | Optional: an order or transaction reference, or why it failed or what you saw. |

## `reconcile_purchase`

Close a reservation whose outcome you reported unknown with settle_purchase, once, from what you checked (the processor's record, the wallet, the seller's order). Paid counts it at the amount paid. Not paid gives the amount back to today's budget, so only the workspace's owner may say so: a workspace-wide key with routing write scope, never an agent's own key. Needs a Last Price credential with price compute scope. Needs a claimed workspace: a sandbox key from self-registration is refused (403) until a person claims the workspace.

- **Access:** key, price compute scope (claimed workspace only: a self-registered sandbox key gets 403)
- **Behaviour:** changes data
- **REST:** `/api/spend-policy/reservations/{id}/reconcile`

| Argument | Type | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `reservation_id` **(required)** | string | reservation.id from check_purchase. |
| `outcome` **(required)** | `paid` / `not_paid` | Whether the money moved. |
| `amount` | number | With paid: what was actually paid, if less than reserved. |
| `note` **(required)** | string | Required: what you checked, e.g. the processor reference. |

## `get_purchase_intent`

Read one buyer intent across every check made under its intent_id: the intent as recorded (source, merchant, maximum, currency, expiry, the evidence hash, and verified, false until Last Price can check the evidence), how many checks were allowed, denied or asked about, and how much of the maximum is held, spent and left. Use it before the next purchase under the same intent. An agent key sees only its own checks. Only where the workspace has intents switched on (else an error with code not_released). Needs a Last Price credential with price compute scope. Needs a claimed workspace: a sandbox key from self-registration is refused (403) until a person claims the workspace.

- **Access:** key, price compute scope (claimed workspace only: a self-registered sandbox key gets 403)
- **Behaviour:** changes data
- **REST:** `/api/spend-policy/intents/{id}`
- **Errors and cautions:** Only where the workspace has intents switched on (else an error with code not_released).

| Argument | Type | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `intent_id` **(required)** | string | The intent_id a check_purchase carried. |

## `open_spend_session`

Before a run of small paid calls to one seller (a stream of x402 calls at a cent each, say), open one budget for the run instead of checking every call. Your owner's spend policy judges the session like a purchase of max_amount: allow holds that maximum against today's cap and returns reservation.id, the session id; ask means a person approves the budget first, then send the same request again; deny means do not start. Then call draw_session_spend right before paying each call, and close_spend_session when done, which gives back what you did not draw. A session left open gives its remainder back when it expires. Only where the workspace has sessions switched on (else an error with code not_released: use check_purchase per purchase). Needs a Last Price credential with price compute scope. Needs a claimed workspace: a sandbox key from self-registration is refused (403) until a person claims the workspace.

- **Access:** key, price compute scope (claimed workspace only: a self-registered sandbox key gets 403)
- **Behaviour:** changes data
- **REST:** `/api/spend-policy/check`
- **Errors and cautions:** Only where the workspace has sessions switched on (else an error with code not_released: use check_purchase per purchase).

| Argument | Type | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `agentid_token` | string | Your AgentID ID token, issued for Last Price, when your owner's policy lets only verified agents spend. Sent as the AgentID-Token header. |
| `seller` **(required)** | string | Who the calls pay: an API, domain or wallet name. |
| `max_amount` **(required)** | number | The most the whole run may spend. |
| `currency` | string | Three-letter ISO currency code. Defaults to USD. |
| `item` | string | Optional: what the calls buy. |
| `category` | string | Optional: its category, when the policy limits or budgets categories. |
| `agent_id` | string | Only with a workspace-wide key: open it on behalf of this agent. An agent key always acts as itself. |
| `ttl_seconds` | integer | How long the session stays open, in seconds. Defaults to 3600. |
| `intent` | object | Optional: what the buyer approved for this purchase, from an American Express intent, an AP2 intent mandate, or declared by you. A purchase that names another seller, costs more than max_amount (counting every purchase under the same intent_id), is in another currency or comes after expires_at is denied, whatever the policy allows. evidence (the token or mandate) is kept only as a hash and is not verified yet. Only where the workspace has intents switched on (else an error with code not_released). |

## `draw_session_spend`

Right before you pay for one call in a session open_spend_session opened, draw the call's price from it. drawn true: pay for the call now. An error means do not pay for this call: the draws would pass the session's maximum (remaining says what is left), this one call costs more than the policy allows per purchase, your owner changed the policy and the session was closed (open a new one if it still allows), or the session is closed or expired. If the call then fails, settle_session_draw with outcome failed gives the draw back. Needs a Last Price credential with price compute scope. Needs a claimed workspace: a sandbox key from self-registration is refused (403) until a person claims the workspace.

- **Access:** key, price compute scope (claimed workspace only: a self-registered sandbox key gets 403)
- **Behaviour:** changes data
- **REST:** `/api/spend-policy/sessions/{id}/draw`
- **Errors and cautions:** An error means do not pay for this call: the draws would pass the session's maximum (remaining says what is left), this one call costs more than the policy allows per purchase, your owner changed the policy and the session was closed (open a new one if it still allows), or the session is closed or expired.

| Argument | Type | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `session_id` **(required)** | string | reservation.id from open_spend_session. |
| `amount` **(required)** | number | This call's price, in the session's currency. |
| `item` | string | Optional: what this call buys. |
| `note` | string | Optional: a request or payment reference. |

## `settle_session_draw`

Say what happened to a call you drew for with draw_session_spend. outcome failed: the payment did not go through, so the draw goes back to the session. outcome unknown: you cannot tell (a timeout, an unreadable answer), so the draw keeps counting until it is reconciled. Then, from what you checked, outcome paid (amount when less than drawn) or not paid, each with a note. Not paid gives budget back, so only the workspace's owner may send it: a workspace-wide key with routing write scope, never an agent's own key. Needs a Last Price credential with price compute scope. Needs a claimed workspace: a sandbox key from self-registration is refused (403) until a person claims the workspace.

- **Access:** key, price compute scope (claimed workspace only: a self-registered sandbox key gets 403)
- **Behaviour:** changes data
- **REST:** `/api/spend-policy/sessions/{id}/draws/{drawId}/settle`

| Argument | Type | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `session_id` **(required)** | string | reservation.id from open_spend_session. |
| `draw_id` **(required)** | string | draw.id from draw_session_spend. |
| `outcome` **(required)** | `failed` / `unknown` / `paid` / `not_paid` | failed or unknown to report the call; paid or not paid to reconcile one reported unknown. |
| `amount` | number | With paid: what was actually paid, if less than drawn. |
| `note` | string | What you saw or checked. Required to reconcile. |

## `get_spend_session`

Read a session: whether it is open, expired or closed, its maximum, what it has drawn and what remains, and its draws, newest first, each drawn, unknown or returned. Use it to resume a run, or to find a draw to settle. Needs a Last Price credential with price compute scope. Needs a claimed workspace: a sandbox key from self-registration is refused (403) until a person claims the workspace.

- **Access:** key, price compute scope (claimed workspace only: a self-registered sandbox key gets 403)
- **Behaviour:** changes data
- **REST:** `/api/spend-policy/sessions/{id}`

| Argument | Type | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `session_id` **(required)** | string | reservation.id from open_spend_session. |

## `close_spend_session`

Close a session when its run of calls is done, once: what you drew counts as spent, and returned says how much of the maximum went back to today's cap. Close as soon as you are done rather than letting it lapse, so the rest of the budget is free for other purchases at once. Needs a Last Price credential with price compute scope. Needs a claimed workspace: a sandbox key from self-registration is refused (403) until a person claims the workspace.

- **Access:** key, price compute scope (claimed workspace only: a self-registered sandbox key gets 403)
- **Behaviour:** changes data
- **REST:** `/api/spend-policy/sessions/{id}/close`

| Argument | Type | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `session_id` **(required)** | string | reservation.id from open_spend_session. |
| `note` | string | Optional: why the run ended. |

## `get_offer_settings`

Read how your workspace takes offers and counter-offers from buyers: whether offers are on, your public handle, the rounds, concession and expiry limits, the products open to offers with their list and floor prices, the last 30 days' negotiations, and the public URLs a buyer's agent uses. Needs a Last Price credential with routing read scope. Needs a claimed workspace: a sandbox key from self-registration is refused (403) until a person claims the workspace.

- **Access:** key, routing read scope (claimed workspace only: a self-registered sandbox key gets 403)
- **Behaviour:** changes data
- **REST:** `/api/negotiation/settings`

_No arguments._

## `set_offer_settings`

Turn offers and counter-offers on or off for your workspace and set the schedule every negotiation runs on. Omitted fields keep their saved value, or the default. A handle another workspace holds is refused. Needs a Last Price credential with routing write scope. Needs a claimed workspace: a sandbox key from self-registration is refused (403) until a person claims the workspace.

- **Access:** key, routing write scope (claimed workspace only: a self-registered sandbox key gets 403)
- **Behaviour:** changes data
- **REST:** `/api/negotiation/settings`
- **Errors and cautions:** A handle another workspace holds is refused.

| Argument | Type | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `enabled` **(required)** | boolean | Whether buyers can make offers to your workspace at all. Off by default. |
| `handle` | string | Your public handle: 3 to 40 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens. |
| `max_rounds` | integer | Most offers a buyer may make in one negotiation. |
| `concession_rate` | number | How far each counter moves toward the buyer, between 0 and 1. |
| `min_offer_ratio` | number | Offers below this share of the list price are rejected outright. |
| `offer_ttl_minutes` | integer | How long a counter stands before it expires, in minutes. |
| `daily_negotiation_cap` | integer | Most new negotiations a day. |

## `set_offer_product`

Open one product to offers, or change it: this saves the product whole (create or replace). Buyers see the list price and never the floor price, which is never breached; the floor cannot exceed the list price. Each product has its own switch, off unless you set enabled. Needs a Last Price credential with routing write scope. Needs a claimed workspace: a sandbox key from self-registration is refused (403) until a person claims the workspace.

- **Access:** key, routing write scope (claimed workspace only: a self-registered sandbox key gets 403)
- **Behaviour:** changes data
- **REST:** `/api/negotiation/products`

| Argument | Type | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `product_id` **(required)** | string | Your own id for the product, as buyers name it in an offer. |
| `title` | string / null | A name for your own reference. |
| `enabled` **(required)** | boolean | Whether buyers can make offers on this product. |
| `list_price` **(required)** | number | The asking price buyers see. |
| `floor_price` **(required)** | number | The lowest price you will accept. Never shown to buyers. |
| `unit_cost` | number / null | Your cost per unit, read by the margin and cost guardrails. |
| `currency` | string | A three letter ISO 4217 code. Defaults to USD. |
| `max_rounds` | integer / null | Rounds for this product, instead of the workspace setting. |

## `remove_offer_product`

Take a product off offers. Negotiations already open on it stop, because a product that is not listed answers buyers with not found. Needs a Last Price credential with routing write scope. Needs a claimed workspace: a sandbox key from self-registration is refused (403) until a person claims the workspace.

| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `product_id` **(required)** | string | Your own id for the product, as buyers name it in an offer. |

Try an offer against one of your own products and see the answer a buyer would get (accept, counter or reject), with the limits behind it. Nothing is recorded and nobody is bound, and it works while offers are off, so you can check your terms first. Needs a Last Price credential with price compute scope. Needs a claimed workspace: a sandbox key from self-registration is refused (403) until a person claims the workspace.

- **Access:** key, price compute scope (claimed workspace only: a self-registered sandbox key gets 403)
- **Behaviour:** changes data

| `previous_counter` | number | The counter you made in the round before, if any. |

## `list_negotiations`

Your workspace's negotiations, newest first: what a buyer sees plus the floor and asking price each one opened with. Use it to honour an accepted price at checkout: find the negotiation and charge its agreed price. Needs a Last Price credential with routing read scope. Needs a claimed workspace: a sandbox key from self-registration is refused (403) until a person claims the workspace.

- **Behaviour:** changes data

| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `status` | `open` / `accepted` / `rejected` / `expired` | Only negotiations in this state. |
| `limit` | integer | How many to return. Defaults to 50. |

## `get_offer_terms`

Read a seller's negotiable terms by their public handle: which products are open to offers, at what list price and currency, how many offers a negotiation allows and how long a counter stands. Never the floor price. Pass product_id to narrow it to one product. Public: needs no credential. An unknown handle, a seller with offers off and a product that is off all answer not found.

- **Access:** no key needed (answers from a public demo without one; a key gives your own workspace)
- **Behaviour:** changes data

| Argument | Type | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `handle` **(required)** | string | The seller's public handle, from the terms they publish. |
| `product_id` | string | The seller's id for the product. |

## `make_offer`

Name a price for a seller's product and get the answer: accept, counter or reject, with the price and the reason. The first offer opens a negotiation and returns a buyer token, once: keep it. To make the next offer in the same negotiation, pass negotiation_id and buyer_token too. buyer_ref is an optional opaque reference for the seller and never a name or email. The seller's floor is never breached or shown. Public: needs no credential, and it is limited per address and by the rounds the seller allows.

- **Access:** no key needed (answers from a public demo without one; a key gives your own workspace)
- **Behaviour:** changes data
- **Errors and cautions:** Public: needs no credential, and it is limited per address and by the rounds the seller allows.

| Argument | Type | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `handle` **(required)** | string | The seller's public handle, from the terms they publish. |
| `product_id` **(required)** | string | The seller's id for the product. |
| `offered_price` **(required)** | number | The price you offer, in the seller's currency. |
| `negotiation_id` | string | The negotiation id from the first answer. |
| `buyer_token` | string | The buyer token the first answer gave you, once. Keep it: it is the only way back into the negotiation. |
| `buyer_ref` | string | An opaque reference for the seller's bookkeeping. Never a name or email. |

## `get_negotiation`

Read your own negotiation with a seller: its status, the rounds used and left, the standing counter, the agreed price and the history. Needs the negotiation id and the buyer token the negotiation opened with, not an account. A wrong token and a missing negotiation answer the same not found. Public: needs no credential.

- **Access:** no key needed (answers from a public demo without one; a key gives your own workspace)
- **Behaviour:** changes data

| Argument | Type | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `handle` **(required)** | string | The seller's public handle, from the terms they publish. |
| `negotiation_id` **(required)** | string | The negotiation id from the first answer. |
| `buyer_token` **(required)** | string | The buyer token the first answer gave you, once. Keep it: it is the only way back into the negotiation. |

## `accept_counter`

Take the seller's standing counter: the negotiation closes as accepted at that price. This commits the buyer to the price, so call it only when you mean to buy at it. A counter past its time, a closed negotiation, or a counter the seller can no longer allow answers with a conflict and binds nothing. Needs the negotiation id and the buyer token. Public: needs no credential.

- **Access:** no key needed (answers from a public demo without one; a key gives your own workspace)
- **Behaviour:** changes data

| Argument | Type | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `handle` **(required)** | string | The seller's public handle, from the terms they publish. |
| `negotiation_id` **(required)** | string | The negotiation id from the first answer. |
| `buyer_token` **(required)** | string | The buyer token the first answer gave you, once. Keep it: it is the only way back into the negotiation. |

Read Last Price's Universal Commerce Protocol business profile: the services, capabilities and payment handlers a UCP agent discovers before it shops here. Public: needs no credential.

_No arguments._

## `get_ucp_quote`

Price a cart the UCP way: pass cart with line_items, and optionally request_id, function_id, routing_preference, currency, stage (quote, cart, checkout or order), checkout, order, payment, context and agentid_token. It routes the cart through the pricing network and answers a UCP quote. Pass agentid_token (an AgentID ID token issued for Last Price) to be recorded as a verified buying agent; the answer then names you, marked verified. Needs a Last Price credential with price compute scope. Needs a claimed workspace: a sandbox key from self-registration is refused (403) until a person claims the workspace.

- **Access:** key, price compute scope (claimed workspace only: a self-registered sandbox key gets 403)
- **Behaviour:** changes data
- **REST:** `/api/ucp/quote`

| Argument | Type | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `cart` **(required)** | object | The cart to price. |
| `request_id` | string | Your id for this request. |
| `function_id` | string | The pricing function to use. |
| `routing_preference` | `cheapest` / `fastest` / `explicit` / `round_robin` / `weighted` / `policy` / `default` | How to pick a function when none is named. |
| `currency` | string | The currency to price in. |
| `stage` | `quote` / `cart` / `checkout` / `order` | Where in the funnel the quote is for. Defaults to quote. |
| `checkout` | object | Checkout details. |
| `order` | object | Order details. |
| `payment` | object | Payment details. |
| `context` | object | Anything that shapes the price: product type, country, channel. |
| `agentid_token` | string | Optional: your AgentID ID token (from auth.agentid.com, issued for Last Price), sent as the AgentID-Token header so the quote records you as a verified buying agent. Leave it out to buy unverified. |

## `create_ucp_checkout`

Open a UCP checkout session: pass line_items, and optionally buyer, context, payment, signals, cart_id, fulfillment, discounts, currency, idempotency_key and agentid_token. Pass the same idempotency_key with the same body to retry safely: you get the first session back instead of a second one. Pass agentid_token to have the session record you as a verified buying agent. It answers the session with its id and status. Needs a Last Price credential with price compute scope. Needs a claimed workspace: a sandbox key from self-registration is refused (403) until a person claims the workspace.

- **Access:** key, price compute scope (claimed workspace only: a self-registered sandbox key gets 403)
- **Behaviour:** changes data
- **REST:** `/api/ucp/checkout-sessions`

| Argument | Type | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `line_items` **(required)** | array | What is being bought. |
| `buyer` | object | Who is buying. |
| `context` | object | Where the checkout happens: locale, country, channel and the like. |
| `payment` | object | The payment handler and currency. |
| `signals` | object | Where the buyer came from: referrer, utm values and device type. |
| `fulfillment` | object | How the order is fulfilled: its methods. |
| `discounts` | object | Discount codes to apply. |
| `cart_id` | string | The cart this checkout comes from. |
| `currency` | string | The currency. Defaults to the first line item's, or USD. |
| `idempotency_key` | string | Your key for this checkout. Retrying with the same key and body returns the first session; the same key with a different body is refused. |
| `agentid_token` | string | Optional: your AgentID ID token (from auth.agentid.com, issued for Last Price), sent as the AgentID-Token header so the quote records you as a verified buying agent. Leave it out to buy unverified. |

## `add_storefront_dns_record`

Add a DNS record to a domain your workspace registered through Last Price, to use it for more than the storefront: MX for email, TXT for SPF, DKIM, DMARC or site verification, CNAME or A for a subdomain. name is relative (blog for blog.<domain>, empty for the domain itself). Records the storefront needs cannot be replaced. Needs a Last Price credential with workspace settings write scope. Needs a claimed workspace: a sandbox key from self-registration is refused (403) until a person claims the workspace.

- **Access:** key, workspace settings write scope (claimed workspace only: a self-registered sandbox key gets 403)
- **Behaviour:** changes data
- **REST:** `/api/storefronts/{storefrontId}/domains/{domainId}/dns-records`

| Argument | Type | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `storefront_id` **(required)** | string | The storefront id, from list_storefronts. |
| `domain_id` **(required)** | string | The domain id, from list_storefronts or add_storefront_domain. |
| `name` **(required)** | string | Relative name: blog for blog.<domain>, empty for the domain itself. |
| `type` **(required)** | `A` / `AAAA` / `CNAME` / `MX` / `TXT` / `CAA` / `SRV` | The record type. |
| `value` **(required)** | string | The record value, such as a mail server or a target host. |
| `ttl` | integer | Seconds to cache it. |
| `mx_priority` | integer | MX only. Defaults to 10. |

## `check_agent_readiness`

Run the free agent-ready check on a store: pass url, the store address. It reports whether shopping agents can check out, whether bot blocking is in the way and whether margin survives an agent's cut. It fetches the store, so it is limited per address and answers 404 while the check is not released. Public: needs no credential.

- **Access:** no key needed (answers from a public demo without one; a key gives your own workspace)
- **Behaviour:** changes data
- **REST:** `/api/public/agent-ready-check`
- **Errors and cautions:** It fetches the store, so it is limited per address and answers 404 while the check is not released.

| Argument | Type | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `url` **(required)** | string | The store address to check. |

## `list_feature_launches`

List every launch kit for a feature built behind a release flag, for Last Price staff only: the flag's state, readiness (how many checks pass, warn and fail, and what blocks), the go code, what is scheduled, whether the launcher is on, and the release flags that have no kit yet. Read only: it never switches, schedules or sends anything; launching needs the owner's go code through the launch command. Needs an API key holding the launches:read scope by name, made by someone who is still Last Price staff, sent as x-api-key or as Authorization: Bearer lp_...; any other credential gets 404. Needs a claimed workspace: a sandbox key from self-registration is refused (403) until a person claims the workspace.

_No arguments._

## `get_changelog`

What changed in Last Price: the newest release notes, optionally for one feature, written for agents as well as people. Pass feature (a tag such as billing, webhooks, mcp, agent-payments, approvals) to follow one part of the product, and since (YYYY-MM-DD, for example the date you last checked) to see only newer notes. Each note has its date, title, summary, category, feature tags, a link to the full note and, when there is one, the docs section and app screen it is about. Public: needs no credential. Check it at the start of a session and before changing integration code.

- **Access:** no key needed (answers from a public demo without one; a key gives your own workspace)
- **Behaviour:** changes data

| Argument | Type | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `feature` | string | A feature tag slug, for example billing. Omit for every feature. |
| `since` | string | Only notes dated after this day (YYYY-MM-DD). |
| `audience` | `agents` / `users` | Only notes written for this audience. Omit for both. |
| `limit` | integer | How many notes at most, newest first. |

## `list_reels`

List the reels: short recipes for real tasks done with Last Price (price a SaaS seat, check a vendor quote, find an offer for a task), with the tools each one calls. A reel is the agent-readable alternative to a demo video: read one with get_reel and it runs live. Public: needs no credential. Until it is switched on it answers not released.

- **Access:** no key needed (answers from a public demo without one; a key gives your own workspace)
- **Behaviour:** changes data
- **REST:** `/api/public/reels`
- **Errors and cautions:** Until it is switched on it answers not released.

_No arguments._

## `get_reel`

Run a reel live and read its transcript: each step's tool, arguments, status, time and answer, the outcome in one line, and an Ed25519 signature over the transcript checkable at /.well-known/quote-keys.json when signing is configured. Every read is a fresh run on the keyless demo, so it shows what the API answers now, not a recording. It spends your own demo allowance. Public: needs no credential. Until it is switched on it answers not released.

- **Access:** no key needed (answers from a public demo without one; a key gives your own workspace)
- **Behaviour:** changes data
- **REST:** `/api/public/reels/{id}`
- **Errors and cautions:** Until it is switched on it answers not released.

| Argument | Type | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `reel_id` **(required)** | `price-a-saas-seat` / `check-a-vendor-quote` / `find-an-offer-for-a-task` | Which reel to run; list_reels lists them. |

## `simulate_agent_cut`

Simulate how much of a sale to offer an agent platform (a shopping agent or agent marketplace that charges sellers a cut) if it ranks sellers partly by the cut they pay. No platform publishes such a ranking, so this is a simulation under your assumption (visibility_per_point_pct: percent more channel sales per extra point of cut), also run at half, double and zero of it. Returns the profit at each cut, the recommended cut, the cut with the smallest worst case, the break-even, and a channel rate ready for PUT /api/channel-rates. Changes nothing. Answers 404 until the cut advisor is switched on for your workspace. Needs a Last Price credential with routing read scope. Needs a claimed workspace: a sandbox key from self-registration is refused (403) until a person claims the workspace.

- **Access:** key, routing read scope (claimed workspace only: a self-registered sandbox key gets 403)
- **Behaviour:** changes data
- **REST:** `/api/cut-advisor`
- **Errors and cautions:** Answers 404 until the cut advisor is switched on for your workspace.

| Argument | Type | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `price` **(required)** | number | Your own price before any channel cut. |
| `unit_cost` **(required)** | number | What one unit costs you, same currency. |
| `current_cut_pct` **(required)** | number | The cut the channel takes today, in percent. |
| `base_units` **(required)** | number | Units sold through the channel per period at the current cut. |
| `visibility_per_point_pct` | number | Your assumption: percent more channel sales per extra point of cut. Defaults to 2. |
| `passed_on_pct` | number | How much of the cut is added to the price, in percent. Defaults to 100. |
| `price_elasticity` | number | How channel buyers respond to price. Defaults to -1.5. |
| `max_visibility_change_pct` | number | Most ranking can move channel sales, in percent either way. Defaults to 100. |
| `min_cut_pct` | number | Lowest cut to try. Defaults to 2.5 (or the current cut, if lower). |
| `max_cut_pct` | number | Highest cut to try. Defaults to 30 (or the current cut, if higher). |
| `step_pct` | number | Gap between the cuts tried. Defaults to 0.5. |
| `channel` | string | The channel name, as you save it in channel rates (e.g. instinct). |
| `currency` | string | ISO 4217 code of price and unit_cost, echoed back. |

## `get_cut_advisor_settings`

Read the settings behind simulate_agent_cut: whether the cut advisor is released for your workspace, the defaults it applies and the limits on each input. Free to call; read it before simulate_agent_cut to see what it will accept. Needs a Last Price credential. - **Access:** key (claimed workspace only: a self-registered sandbox key gets 403)
- **Behaviour:** changes data
- **REST:** `/api/cut-advisor`

_No arguments._
